n169b7fd38b6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about regions of high population density in India?
o: The Ganga plain is densely populated owing to fertile alluvial soils
The Ganges–Brahmaputra delta is among the world's densely populated regions
Intensive agriculture and water support the density of the Ganga plain
The Thar desert has very high density owing to fertile alluvium
n169b7fd38b6.x: The Thar desert is not a high-density region; the Ganga plain and Ganges–Brahmaputra delta are, owing to fertile alluvium, water and intensive agriculture.

n0cb1df45bf2.s: Which of the following pairs (region – population-resource type) is correctly matched?
o: Ganga-Yamuna Doab and Coastal Odisha – Progressive
Ganga-Yamuna Doab and Tamil Nadu – Progressive
n0cb1df45bf2.x: The Ganga-Yamuna Doab and Tamil Nadu are progressive (resource-developed) regions; Coastal Odisha and Rajasthan are not.

nc95f46eca87.s: Because Census 2021 was postponed, Census 2027 will come how many years after Census 2011?
nc95f46eca87.x: The delay of the 2021 Census makes Census 2027 the next Census, 16 years after Census 2011.

n2e32cef0732.s: India's population density rose from 117 persons per sq km in 1951 to ____ in Census 2011.
n2e32cef0732.x: Density rose from 117 (1951) to 382 persons per sq km in 2011; 304 is Andhra Pradesh's density.

n70a2ff43526.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: 106th Amendment – Delimitation freeze till the first census after 2026
84th Amendment – Delimitation freeze till the first census after 2026
Article 334A – Delimitation freeze till the first census after 2026
n70a2ff43526.x: The delimitation freeze till the first census after 2026 is linked to the 84th Amendment; the 106th Amendment and Article 334A concern women's reservation.

ne666af8ffea.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the population of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Its density in 2011 (304) was lower than India's average (382)
Its population was about 233 lakh in 1961
The doubling of its population since 1961 explains why its density is below India's average
ne666af8ffea.x: Both the density gap and the doubling of population are true, but the doubling does not explain why AP's density is below India's average.

n6b8326e3b7b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about population density as per Census 2011?
o: Sikkim had a lower density than Mizoram
Arunachal Pradesh had a density of 17 per sq km
Andaman and Nicobar Islands had a density of 46 per sq km
Mizoram had a density of 52 per sq km
n6b8326e3b7b.x: Sikkim (86) was denser than Mizoram (52); the ascending order is Arunachal Pradesh (17), Andaman and Nicobar (46), Mizoram (52), Sikkim (86).

ndf232638a06.s: Which of the following pairs (stage of demographic transition – position) is correctly matched?
ndf232638a06.x: The sequence is high stationary, early expanding, late expanding, low stationary and declining, so early expanding is the second stage.

n59f82a665b0.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 placed the peak of India's demographic dividend around:
n59f82a665b0.x: ES 2025-26 placed the peak around 2030 (about 65% aged 15-59); 2041 was the ES 2018-19 estimate.

nacdceac69c0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh and the demographic dividend?
o: It combines a 9.21% growth rate with a large youth workforce
Its dividend rests exclusively on a rising elderly population
Its literacy rate of 67.35% remains a concern
Its large youth workforce supports a demographic dividend
nacdceac69c0.x: A dividend rests on the working-age, not the elderly, population; AP pairs a 9.21% growth rate and a large youth workforce with lagging 67.35% literacy.

n0c95824a21c.s: Andhra Pradesh is ageing faster than India mainly because of its:
o: Large youth workforce and 9.21% growth rate
High TFR and low median age
Low TFR (1.5) and high median age (32.5)
n0c95824a21c.x: Low fertility (TFR 1.5) and a relatively high median age (32.5) explain why AP is ageing faster than India.

new.s: As per Census 2011, the population density of India was:
new.x: India's density was 382 per sq km in 2011, up from 325 in 2001.

new.s: Which was the most densely populated State of India in Census 2011?
new.x: Bihar was the densest State, with over 1,100 persons per sq km.

new.s: Which Union Territory had the highest population density in Census 2011?
new.x: NCT of Delhi (over 11,000 per sq km) was the densest UT, followed by Chandigarh.

new.s: Which State had the lowest population density (17 per sq km) in Census 2011?
new.x: Arunachal Pradesh was the sparsest State at 17 persons per sq km.

new.s: Among these southern States, which had the lowest population density in Census 2011?
new.x: Undivided AP had 308, below Karnataka (319), Tamil Nadu (555) and Kerala (860).

new.s: Agricultural density is calculated as:
new.x: Agricultural density counts only farm people per unit of net cultivable area; physiological density uses all people per net cultivated area.

new.s: Which of the following is sparsely populated mainly because of a lack of water?
new.x: Water draws people to river valleys, while the dry Thar desert remains sparsely populated.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about factors of population distribution in India:
1. Loamy alluvial soils support dense population.
2. Thin, rocky soils support dense population.
3. Plains are more densely populated than hills and mountains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Loamy alluvium and plains support dense population; thin, rocky soils are linked with sparse population.

new.s: The Godavari-Krishna coastal deltas are densely populated mainly because of:
new.x: The Godavari-Krishna deltas support dense population through intensive rice farming; mining explains Dhanbad's density.

new.s: In population-resource regions, a region where resources exceed their use is called a:
new.x: A deficit region is one where resources exceed use; a problem region has population pressure on limited resources.

new.s: Population pressure on limited or degraded resources characterises which population-resource region?
new.x: A problem region has population pressure on limited or degraded resources.

new.s: Which of the following States is NOT part of the BIMARU group?
new.x: BIMARU stands for Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh; Odisha is not one of them.

new.s: Which was the least populous State of India in Census 2011?
new.x: Sikkim (6.08 lakh) was the least populous State, followed by Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Nagaland.

new.s: The smallest State of India by area is:
new.x: Goa is the smallest State by area; Lakshadweep is the smallest Union Territory.

new.s: The smallest district of India by area is:
new.x: Mahe in Puducherry is the smallest district by area.

new.s: To be a Census Town, a settlement must have a population density of at least:
new.x: A Census Town needs at least 5,000 people, a density of 400 per sq km and 75% male non-farm workers.

new.s: India's first census, a non-synchronous one, was held in 1872 under:
new.x: The first census of 1872 was non-synchronous, under Lord Mayo; the first synchronous census of 1881 was under Lord Ripon.

new.s: Census 2011 was India's ____ census since 1872.
new.x: Census 2011 was the 15th census since 1872 and the 7th after Independence.

new.s: The subject 'Census' is placed in which list of the Seventh Schedule?
o: None; it is a residuary subject
new.x: Census is Entry 69 of the Union List and is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.

new.s: Census 2027 will be India's first census that is:
new.x: Census 2027 will be the first digital census, mobile-app based with self-enumeration, and the first caste count beyond SC/ST since Independence.

new.s: Phase I (House Listing and Housing Census) of Census 2027 is held during:
new.x: The House Listing phase runs from 1 April to 30 September 2026; population enumeration follows in February 2027.

new.s: India's share of the world's area is about:
new.x: India has 2.4% of the world's area but about 17.7% of its population.

new.s: According to UN DESA, India overtook China as the most populous country in:
new.x: UN DESA reported that India overtook China in April 2023.

new.s: The Technical Group on Population Projections projects India's population at 1,522.3 million by:
new.x: The Technical Group (MoHFW) projects 1,363.0 million in 2021 rising to 1,522.3 million by 2036.

new.s: The 'steady growth' phase of India's population, when mortality fell but the birth rate stayed high, was:
new.x: Phase II (1921-1951) saw steady growth as health, sanitation and transport reduced mortality.

new.s: The average annual exponential growth rate of India's population in Census 2011 was:
new.x: The average annual exponential growth rate was 1.64%; 17.7% was the decadal growth.

new.s: As per Census 2011, persons aged 60 and above formed about what share of India's population?
new.x: The elderly (60+) were 8.6% in 2011, up from 5.6% in 1961; 9.7% is the SRS 2024 figure.

new.s: Which State had the highest share of elderly population in Census 2011?
new.x: Kerala had the highest elderly share (12.6%) and Jharkhand the lowest (7.1%).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's age structure as per SRS 2024:
1. The 15-59 age group forms 66.4% of the population.
2. Persons aged 60 and above form 9.7%.
3. The 0-14 age group forms 34%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: SRS 2024 puts 15-59 at 66.4% and 60+ at 9.7%; the 0-14 share is 24%, not 34%.

new.s: Natural increase of population is the difference between:
new.x: Natural increase is births minus deaths; net migration is in-migrants minus out-migrants.

new.s: Actual growth of population equals:
new.x: Actual growth is natural increase plus net migration.

new.s: Which State recorded the highest decadal population growth during 2001-11?
new.x: Meghalaya (27.9%) was highest, followed by Arunachal Pradesh (26.0%); Nagaland was the only State with negative growth.

new.s: Which Union Territory recorded the highest decadal population growth during 2001-11?
new.x: Dadra and Nagar Haveli (55.9%) had the highest UT growth; Lakshadweep (6.3%) had the lowest.

new.s: The term 'BIMARU' was coined by:
new.x: Demographer Ashish Bose coined BIMARU (1986) for Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: The literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh in Census 2011 was:
new.x: AP's literacy was 67.35%; 72.98% is India's rate and 59.96% is AP's female literacy.

new.s: The sex ratio of Andhra Pradesh as per Census 2011 was:
new.x: AP's sex ratio in 2011 was 997.

new.s: The medium-term objective of the National Population Policy 2000 was to bring TFR to 2.1 by:
new.x: NPP 2000 set TFR 2.1 (replacement level) by 2010 as its medium-term objective.

new.s: The long-term objective of the National Population Policy 2000 is a stable population by:
new.x: NPP 2000's long-term objective is population stabilisation by 2045.

new.s: The immediate objective of the National Population Policy 2000 is to:
o: Meet the unmet need for contraception
new.x: Its immediate objective is to meet the unmet need for contraception, health infrastructure and personnel.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched about the National Population Policy 2000?
o: Immediate objective – meeting unmet need for contraception
new.x: The long-term objective is a stable population by 2045; TFR 2.1 was the medium-term target for 2010.

new.s: Under the National Population Policy 2000, replacement-level TFR was targeted by:
new.x: NPP 2000's medium-term objective was TFR 2.1 by 2010; 2045 is the target for a stable population.

new.s: The demographic transition theory was first put forward in 1929 by:
new.x: Warren Thompson proposed it in 1929; Frank Notestein later gave the formal three-stage version.

new.s: 'The Population Bomb' (1968) was written by:
new.x: Paul Ehrlich's The Population Bomb (1968) warned of mass famine from overpopulation.

new.s: The National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was issued in:
new.x: The National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship dates from 2015; the National Youth Policy is of 2014.

new.s: Uttar Pradesh's draft Population (Control, Stabilization and Welfare) Bill was brought in:
new.x: UP's draft Population (Control, Stabilization and Welfare) Bill dates from 2021.

new.s: As per NFHS-6 (2023-24), which State had the highest TFR?
new.x: NFHS-6 shows Bihar highest (2.7) and Andaman and Nicobar lowest (0.9).

new.s: India launched the world's first national family planning programme in:
new.x: India's national family planning programme of 1952 was the first in the world; it was renamed the Family Welfare Programme in 1977.

new.s: Mission Parivar Vikas (2016) covers how many districts with TFR of 3 or more?
new.x: It covers 146 high-fertility districts in seven States, including UP, Bihar and Rajasthan.

new.s: The dominant contraceptive method among married women in India (NFHS-5) is:
new.x: Female sterilisation dominates, used by 37.9% of married women in NFHS-5.

new.s: The Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI) covers people aged:
new.x: LASI, by IIPS Mumbai for MoHFW, covers people aged 45 and above.

new.s: Around 2020, which country had a median age of about 45?
new.x: Japan's median age was about 45, against 37 for China and the US and 28 for India.
